passages.quote:
Background

This guidance is for employers delivering the child and family Assessed and Supported Year in Employment (ASYE) programme in England.

It explains:

which newly qualified social workers (NQSWs) should be included in the final claims process

how to claim any outstanding ASYE registration payment and the final £1,000 completion payment, including an advance final payment where applicable

the information and documents employers must submit

what employers must do for participants who have not completed by 10 March 2027

what happens after the Department for Education (DfE) ASYE programme closes

The ASYE funding period ends on 31 March 2027. Employers remain responsible for supporting and assessing participants who continue their ASYE after that date.

Key dates

Activity Date

Deadline for claims for new ASYE registrations 1 February 2027

Penultimate claims processing window 2 to 14 February 2027 (for claims submitted up to and including 1 February 2027)

Final claims window opens 22 February 2027

Final deadline for submitting claims 10 March 2027

DfE funded ASYE programme ends 31 March 2027

Final payment date 31 March 2027

The final payment date is 31 March 2027. To allow sufficient time for claims to be checked, assured and processed for payment, employers must submit all final claims and supporting documentation by 10 March 2027.

Claims received after this deadline will not be accepted or processed for payment.

Employers must not wait until a newly qualified social worker (NQSW) has completed the programme before submitting a final claim if their ASYE will continue beyond March 2027.

Funding available

The Department for Education provides up to £2,000 for each eligible NQSW, this consists of:

£1,000 following registration

£1,000 following completion, or through the March 2027 advance payment process where the participant will complete the programme after the final claims deadline

Employers may claim the final £1,000 in advance for eligible participants who have not completed by 10 March 2027, including eligible deferred participants.

An employer cannot claim more than one registration payment and one final payment for the same participant.

Placing participants in categories

Employers should review every NQSW they have registered with DfE and place them into one of the following categories.

Category 1: NQSWs who complete before the final claims window opens on 22 February 2027

Claim route

Employers should submit a normal completion claim through the relevant payment window.

What the employer must provide or do

The claim must include:

the NQSW’s actual completion date

the final assessment outcome

a completed and signed ASYE Completion Declaration and Funding Return

a completed and signed Annex C

the completed application spreadsheet or other claim schedule specified by DfE

The grant offer letter states that the final payment becomes claimable when the employer confirms that the final assessment against the post-qualifying standards has taken place.

The claims require the actual completion date, assessment outcome and signed completion declaration.

Deadline

Submit through the relevant payment window. Any outstanding claim must be submitted by 10 March 2027.

22 February 2027 is the date the final claims window opens, not the submission deadline.

Category 2: NQSWs who will complete during the final claims window - between 22 February to 10 March 2027

Claim route

Submit a normal completion claim.

What the employer must provide or do

Submit the claim using the actual completion information once the final assessment and moderation process is complete.

Do not use the advance payment route if a complete and accurate normal completion claim can be submitted by the final deadline.

Deadline

10 March 2027.

Category 3: NQSWs still undertaking ASYE after 10 March 2027

Claim route

Advance claim for the final £1,000 during the final claims window.

What the employer must provide or do

Include eligible participants who:

started later in the 2026 to 2027 funding year

are progressing through ASYE but have not reached final assessment

have an agreed extension

have deferred and subsequently returned, or are expected to return, to the programme

are completing on a part-time or extended timetable

Confirm that the participant remains on the programme and that the employer will continue to provide the required support, assessment and quality assurance through to completion.

Submit a consolidated Annex D covering all relevant participants completing after 10 March 2027.

Deadline

10 March 2027. Submit the advance claim during the final claims window, which opens on 22 February 2027.

Category 4: NQSWs who have withdrawn

Claim route

Do not claim an advance final payment for a participant who has permanently withdrawn before the final claim is submitted.

What the employer must provide or do

If not already done:

record the withdrawal

notify DfE through the final return

retain the employer’s record of the withdrawal decision

Registration funding will be subject to clawback where:

the NQSW withdraws within the first 4 weeks of starting the programme

the claim is found not to comply with the grant criteria, either by DfE or through DfE dip-sampling

See existing ASYE guidance for full details of the clawback process.

Deadline

Report the withdrawal through the final return by 10 March 2027.

Category 5: NQSWs whose final assessment outcome is fail

Claim route

Normal completion claim once the final assessment and moderation or quality assurance process is complete.

What the employer must provide or do

Report the actual assessment outcome as fail and submit a normal completion claim.

Under the current grant offer letter, the final payment is linked to the final assessment taking place, regardless of whether the NQSW has met the standard.

Do not issue an ASYE completion certificate where the outcome is fail.

Deadline

passages.quote:
cords and assurance

Employers must retain evidence required by the grant agreement and provide it if requested by DfE for assurance or audit.

Employers must retain sufficient evidence to demonstrate that:

the participant was eligible for funding

the participant was registered correctly

ASYE support and assessment were delivered

the final assessment and moderation process was completed

the reported outcome is accurate

funding was used in accordance with the grant agreement

personal data was managed appropriately

Evidence may include:

portfolios

supervision records

direct observations

critical reflections

work products

feedback

assessment records

moderation records

Changes in circumstances after an advance payment

Employers must notify DfE if, after receiving an advance payment and before 31 March 2028 the:

NQSW completes the ASYE programme

NQSW withdraws permanently

employment ends before the programme is completed

NQSW transfers to another employer

employer can no longer deliver the programme

information included in the final claim is found to be inaccurate

Notifications should be sent to CFASYE.queries@education.gov.uk and should include any of the pertinent details from the list of scenarios above along with the NQSW details to enable DfE to locate the record on the database.

Where appropriate, DfE will advise whether any correction, reconciliation or repayment is required under the grant agreement.

New starters after the ASYE registration deadline

This applies to newly qualified social workers who start employment on or after 1 February 2027 and before the Early Career Development Programme (ECDP) begins in September 2027.

During this transition period:

employers should continue to recruit and employ newly qualified social workers during the transition period

newly qualified social workers cannot be registered onto ASYE

employers cannot claim ASYE funding for newly qualified social workers who start during this period

employers should provide appropriate induction, supervision, support and development through their local arrangements

employers and newly qualified social workers should familiarise themselves with the Early career standards and may use them to support professional development before the ECDP starts

the current intention is that eligible social workers who would previously have started ASYE during the transition period will be able to join the first ECDP cohorts

some social workers may therefore experience a gap between starting employment and joining the ECDP

employers should plan to identify eligible social workers and prepare to nominate them once ECDP eligibility, enrolment and funding guidance is published

decisions about probation, pay progression, increased responsibilities and career progression remain the responsibility of individual employers and should be managed in line with local policies and procedures

DfE will publish detailed guidance on ECDP eligibility, enrolment, funding and transition arrangements in the coming months.

DfE also plans to run a series of employer webinars in early 2027 to explain the new arrangements, eligibility requirements and next steps. Further details will be shared, including webinar dates and registration information, as soon as they are available.

Please send all enquiries related to information in this guidance document to CFASYE.queries@education.gov.uk.
